changes.after: An S4 class describes what named pieces of data its objects may hold. Each named piece is a slot with a required type.

before: S4 classes can declare named slots and their classes. methods::setClass defines StudyEntry with a numeric minutes slot. package::name accesses an exported function from that installed package without attaching it to the search path; methods is part of this R installation.

methods::new constructs an S4 object and checks its declared representation. entry@minutes accesses the slot. A numeric slot does not by itself require positive minutes; domain constraints need a validity rule or explicit validation.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
methods::setClass("StudyEntry", slots = c(minutes = "numeric"))
entry <- methods::new("StudyEntry", minutes = 5)
cat(entry@minutes, "\n")
```
Expected output or behavior: 5. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

A StudyEntry must hold numbers in its minutes slot.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
methods::setClass("StudyEntry", slots = c(minutes = "numeric"))
entry <- methods::new("StudyEntry", minutes = 5)
cat(entry@minutes, "\n")
```
The output is `5`. The object accepts five, and the at-sign reads that slot.
Try putting the word five into the numeric slot.
